description: Cybergenic is a browser-based cancer research hypothesis engine. It examines gene co-occurrence and mutual exclusivity in public tumor cohorts, combines statistical evidence with literature, clinical-trial and functional-dependency context, and exposes evidence-linked findings for researcher inspection. Its public observatory, searchable research corpus and methodology describe evidence gates and out-of-sample evaluation. Outputs are research hypotheses, not clinically validated biomarkers or treatment recommendations.

download.note: Every gene pair the scan tested in 50 tumour cohorts (215,069 burden-aware co-occurrence and mutual exclusivity tests), one Parquet file with checksums and a column guide; CC BY-NC 4.0.

function.note: Tests gene co-occurrence and mutual exclusivity across public tumor cohorts with mutation-burden-aware statistics and false-discovery correction, then visualises evidence-linked research hypotheses in an interactive observatory. Literature and functional-dependency evidence provide context; outputs require independent validation.

name: Cybergenic
